title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They try to scare you into acting quickly.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your benefits will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and pay a small fee today."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security number
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly using the number on your Medicare card.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying a package couldn’t be delivered and you need to click a link to reschedule or pay a fee. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information or installs malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to reschedule: [fake link]"
red_flags: Request for payment or personal info
what_to_do: Do not click the link; delete the message and check with the delivery company using their official website.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails pretending to be from the Social Security Administration, saying there is a problem with your account. They ask you to click a link or download an attachment to fix it.
example_message: "We have noticed suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please verify your information by clicking this link."
red_flags: Email asks for personal or financial info
Urgent request to click a link or open an attachment
what_to_do: Do not click any links or download attachments; report the email to the Social Security Administration.

title: Romance Scams on Facebook
how_it_works: Someone befriends you on Facebook, quickly says they love you, and then asks for money for an emergency. They often claim to be working overseas or in the military.
example_message: "I care about you so much, but I need your help. My wallet was stolen and I can't get home. Can you send me money?"
red_flags: Person you’ve never met asks for money
Stories about emergencies or being stuck overseas
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven’t met in person.

title: Tech Support Pop-Up Scam
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying your device is infected and you must call a number for help. The scammer pretends to be from Microsoft or Apple and tries to get remote access to your computer or asks for payment.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pop-up demands you call a number
Asks for payment or remote access
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number; use your regular antivirus software to check your computer.
